key_insight: MANTA lets a multi-agent system adapt its communication topology during inference, so collaboration structure can self-evolve when the current organization is no longer effective.
engineering_relevance: This matters for building more robust agentic AI systems because it enables dynamic routing, role reassignment, and validation control without changing the task interface or agent budget.
method: Initialize a task-conditioned topology from prior structural experience before execution.
Monitor collaboration traces at deployment and apply bounded structural updates when needed.
Adjust roles, links, execution order, information visibility, and validation pathways while preserving the same agents.
evidence_signal: Across five benchmarks covering information seeking, tool use, planning, workflow execution, and mathematical reasoning, MANTA achieved the best average score of 74.0 and outperformed the strongest baseline by 5.8 points, including the top result on PlanCraft.
watch_item: The approach introduces extra online control logic, so stability, update safety, and compute overhead may become important implementation concerns.
paper_title: MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
